artifacts.summary: 10-phase, 17.5-hour sequential refactor stripping FrameOver to three data fields behind class FrameOver.IsRegular, with the topology and counterexample modules, a complete migration table, and a green --wfail build at every phase boundary.

memory_candidates.content: Refactoring a Lean structure's axiom fields into a Prop-valued class is safely sequenced as introduce-alongside-then-retire: (1) add `class S.IsP` whose fields cite the same predicates, plus a blanket `instance (s : S) : s.IsP := <built from the still-present fields>`; (2) migrate every consumer to `[s.IsP]` binders and every constructor to a regular-spelled variant, verifying against a green tree the whole time because the blanket instance still discharges synthesis; (3) delete the fields and the blanket instance in one dedicated phase. The blanket instance is what makes the intermediate states compile, so the risky deletion becomes a phase whose failures are localized compile errors rather than silent meaning changes. Two companions matter: re-export each old field under its ORIGINAL name as a theorem taking the class binder, so consumer text stays byte-identical and no deprecation alias is needed; and check every reducible predicate that quantifies over the structure (here a FrameClass.Sat table feeding `Valid`) because the strip silently widens such quantifiers unless the predicate is redefined to require the class.
